narrative:
The model determined that you have a 25% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, our bank sets a threshold that your application did not meet, which is why your loan was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and the total amount you wanted to borrow. 

Your short six-month repayment period actually worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward approval, as most approved applicants request much longer terms around 19 months. Unfortunately, this positive effect was outweighed by two other important aspects. Having no checking account is relatively common among applicants (59%), yet the model sees this as a clear signal of higher risk compared with those who maintain positive balances. Similarly, while your requested amount of 3,518 DM is only moderately above the average approved loan of about 3,020 DM, it still contributed toward viewing you as higher risk.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude that your application carried too much uncertainty for approval. 

To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a longer-term loan, opening and maintaining a checking account with positive balances for several months before reapplying, and possibly requesting a smaller amount. These steps would directly address the main concerns that affected this decision. (248 words)
